{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings: 8 compliant, 7 deviations and 3 missing clauses. The risk-allocation core of the agreement is unusually good for us. The liability cap (§ 21.1) is mutual, sits at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and carries the full Excluded Claims set; assignment and change of control (§ 24) is asymmetric in our favour; the licence grant (§ 13), warranties (§ 19), Vendor insurance (§ 18), audit rights (§ 22) and the renewal/uplift mechanic (§ 8.2–8.3) all meet the preferred position, and there are no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

The problems are concentrated in the commercial-commitment and exit provisions, and several of them sit in walk-away territory. Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights", with no termination for convenience anywhere in Section 9 to relieve it. Section 7.2 conditions our right to engage another provider on disclosing and matching any better third-party offer — a de facto exclusivity and a Customer-side MFN in one sentence. The duplicate-numbered Section 12.4 provisions impose a 24-month post-term non-compete and an outright 24-month no-hire on us alone. Each of these directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment.

Three clauses the playbook expects are simply absent. There is no indemnification article at all — the outline jumps from Section 19 to Section 21 — even though § 9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5", § 19.4 refers to "indemnified claims" and § 21.3 treats "indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims. There is no termination for convenience, and there is no transition-assistance or data-return obligation; § 16.5 carves Customer Data out of the return/destroy duty and defers to a "Section 11" that does not exist in the document. Section 28.1 also selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, conflicting with the New York exclusive jurisdiction already granted in § 28.2.

Two proposed redlines did not apply cleanly on verification (§ 28.1 governing law and § 12.4 no-hire) and require manual drafting before the mark-up goes back to Vendor.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full Excluded Claims set. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor restricted. Runs in our favour. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 (first clause so numbered) | Disclose-and-match before engaging another provider is de facto exclusivity/ROFR for the full term with no performance exit. Walk-away. Redline applied. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 (with §§ 7.3, 24.4) | No Customer-payable penalty, termination fee or fee acceleration. Take-or-pay addressed under MINCOMMIT only. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) | Grant extends to Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users; paid-up Vendor Technology perpetual. Deliverable ownership handled under IP. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, no system access. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5, 6.2) | Professional/workmanlike plus conformity warranties; hosted conformity for full term; mutual, carved-back disclaimer. |
| Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; outside accepted list and conflicts with New York County jurisdiction in § 28.2. **Redline failed verification — redraft manually.** |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | No indemnity article (outline runs § 19 → § 21) | No Vendor IP or other indemnity; § 9.3 reference to "Section 20.5" is broken. Walk-away. New Section 20 inserted. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, WC as required, term plus one year; insurance does not cap liability. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns every Customer Deliverable; our licence is revocable, non-transferable and term-limited — fails preferred and fallback. Redline applied. |
| Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match better third-party offers; no product, term or comparison limits. Walk-away. Redline applied. |
| Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". Walk-away. Redline applied. |
| Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second clause so numbered) | 24-month post-term ban on competing products/services in any territory, no carve-outs. Walk-away. Redline applied. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees, expressly negating advertising/unsolicited-application carve-outs. Walk-away. **Redline failed verification — redraft manually.** |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (§§ 9.1–9.3 only; no § 9.4) | No convenience right in a three-year term, with § 2.1 stripping reduction/termination rights. Walk-away. New § 9.4 inserted. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.2 (with § 16.5) | No transition-assistance obligation and no Customer Data return or certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. New § 10.3 inserted. |

---

## Walk-away items

These are the positions we should not sign as drafted:

1. **§ 2.1 — three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Multi-year take-or-pay with no exit is the playbook's walk-away position. Our redline limits Fees to Services ordered or used; the fallback offered in comment is a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled by true-up.
2. **§ 7.2 — disclose-and-match obligation (exclusivity and Customer-side MFN).** Restrains our sourcing freedom for the entire term with no product, duration or comparison limits, and contradicts § 12.3.
3. **§ 12.4 (non-compete) — 24-month post-term ban on competing products or services in any territory.** Fails on scope, duration and carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3. Fallback offered: a term-only restriction on a single named product.
4. **§ 12.4 (no-hire) — one-way 24-month outright no-hire on all Vendor employees.** Fallback offered: a narrow mutual 12-month non-solicit with general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs.
5. **No indemnification article.** Absence of a Vendor IP indemnity falls below the fallback and leaves § 9.3, § 19.4 and § 21.3 cross-referencing obligations that do not exist.
6. **No termination for convenience** in a three-year term where § 2.1 expressly removes reduction and termination rights.
7. **§ 28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Exclusive foreign venue outside the accepted list, and inconsistent with § 28.2.

Also below the fallback, though not flagged as walk-away: **§ 14.2** (Vendor ownership of Customer Deliverables with only a revocable, term-limited licence) and the **absence of any transition-assistance or data-return obligation**, which currently leaves our data with no guaranteed retrieval path.

---

## Next steps

1. **Redraft the two failed redlines manually** before the mark-up is sent: § 28.1 (New York law, delete the Singapore forum, and align the § 28.2 injunction carve-out with the New York County courts) and § 12.4 (delete the one-way 24-month no-hire, with the mutual 12-month fallback in comment).
2. **Confirm the inserted clauses read correctly in context** — new Section 20 (Vendor defence/indemnity with claim procedure, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in 20.5, and a narrow Customer indemnity), new § 9.4 (Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund) and new § 10.3 (up to six months' transition assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days, certified deletion).
3. **Flag the duplicate section numbering to Vendor.** There are two clauses numbered 7.2 and two numbered 12.4; renumbering is needed so our deletions and amendments are unambiguous.
4. **Ask Vendor to fix the broken cross-references:** § 9.3 points to "Section 20.5" and § 16.5 defers to "Sections 11 and 15", but no Section 11 exists in the document. Our new Section 20 restores the first of these.
5. **Use § 12.3 as the lever on the commitment cluster.** Vendor has already acknowledged there that we made no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment; §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 should be conformed to it.
6. **Confirm with the business** the annual spend expectation, the intended commitment term and whether Customer ownership of Deliverables (§ 14.2) is required for this engagement, so we can hold the preferred position or settle at the stated fallbacks.
7. **No action required** on the eight compliant items; we should preserve the favourable terms in §§ 21, 24, 8.3, 18, 19 and 22 as-is during negotiation."}
